claim: Each check the file tells is the one binary (living, coupling, resolving) met at one face of a sentence, and never a rule.
missing: the file joins a check to the binary at one place (a sentence adding nothing releases *at that binary*, EXP 2.1). The span bold (2.4), supplying (3.4), clocking (3.5), a running asked to be one of its faces (3.8), incohering's one catch (3.13), the method's own move (4.5) and one telling deriving from another (4.7) are each said at no face of living, coupling or resolving.
would_close: A link per check naming the face it meets (living, coupling or resolving) and the sign it returns there; or the claim scoped to the checks so joined.

claim: Six protecting run between explaining and naming, three each way; drop one and a phase of the writing runs bare.
missing: *six or none* (NI 3.2) and *drop one and a phase runs bare* are said, not supplied; and the joining of the six between a self and its surface (NI) to the six between explaining and naming (EXP) is shown at no link.
would_close: A link naming each of the six between explaining and naming as one of NI 3.2's couplings at one direction, and a showing that with one removed a phase carries no protecting (a check at a writing, or the necessity taken plainly as a premise).

claim: A sentence carries no birth: no existing thing is put into existing.
missing: no birth needs the converse, that each existing thing's now is the next of a prior existing; F25 does not supply it. NAM 5.40 names *arising* as a living self's own carrying establishing, a relation, and leaves the converse unsaid.
would_close: The converse taken as a premise (each now is the next of a prior existing), or a link from F13's determinacy and reachability giving each momentary a prior as well as a next.

claim: Incohering enters six ways, and one check at the sentence meets them.
missing: the one check is F39 at a file (X7); that incohering enters these six ways and no seventh is not supplied. The count six runs (X148).
would_close: A parting of 'a middle carried across' into its kinds (ground, doer, magnitude, record, explanation, frozen side) shown whole, or the claim said at the six named with the check as the catch for any further way.

claim: A meeting side catches the supplying and a writing side catches the freeze, and neither catches its own.
missing: supplying is invisible from inward of the writing (X20), which supplies the writing side's half; the meeting side's own uncaught is named at no sentence, so *neither* rests on one side.
would_close: A link naming the meeting side's own uncaught and showing it invisible from that side, as EXP 3.4 does for supplying.

claim: Surgical-method's running is no other possible: completing six forward without landing, looping or forking.
missing: the six forward is not supplied (X72), and no link excludes another running completing without landing, looping or forking.
would_close: An enumeration of runnings at the stated conditions (count in and out, along the plane, closing in the other order) showing one completes; or the claim scoped to the stated conditions as a necessity at premises.

claim: Five taken two ways at a self and the couplings among five at a society are one ten arriving twice.
missing: the counts agree (run: 2 × 5 = 10 = C(5, 2)); the deriving of the couplings among five from the five taken two ways is shown at no link, and by the binary of X42 a count agreeing is no joining.
would_close: A correspondence taking each of the ten positions of the two fives (F20) to one coupling of a pair among five, one to one, by one stated rule.

claim: The next interesting is the only next carrying each existing thing on.
missing: the *only* and the *each existing thing* are not supplied: interest is said of a self meeting a telling, and no link joins it to a non-living thing's next (F44) or excludes another next.
would_close: A definition of the next interesting at each existing thing (living and non-living) and a link showing each next carrying a thing on is that one; or the claim scoped to a self meeting a telling.

claim: A naming's four boundings (self-bounding, self-stilling, self-orienting, orthogonalizing) are existing at four faces, the four of the eight.
missing: F51's four boundings of a self are arriving +1, carrying −1, the sign inverting at the membrane and competency asymmetry; a naming's four are bounding, stilling, orienting and orthogonalizing. No link joins the two fours one to one, and no link gives four and no fifth.
would_close: A link pairing each of the naming's four with one of F51's four by one stated relation, and the count four supplied (for example from the four joint forms of two signs, F58).

claim: The family of a still thing's name given to a running thing has three faces and no fourth (landing, standard, reading); a face caught at one word is the whole family caught.
missing: the three faces answer a self's offering, carrying and sign-taking; that a self has these three and no fourth to be reached ahead of is not supplied (R9's three reads of a carrying are another three), nor that one face caught is the family caught. NAM 5.26 says the same three and no fourth.
would_close: A link giving a self's own three (offering, carrying, taking a sign) as all a self has at a coupling, from the resolver's names (2-self-offering, 3-self-carrying, 14-social-crossing), with each face joined to one.

claim: An unfolding is six forward, three own-forward steps at each side, and six lines complete it.
missing: F19 gives each side five positions, prior opening to next opening, two own-forward steps; three own-forward steps at each side, and so the six, are not supplied, nor that an unfolding completes at six and at no other count. X39 and GIM 3.3's six recursions rest here.
would_close: A link giving three own-forward steps at each side (for example the self's openings 1, 3, 5, 7 at one to nine, F31) and a showing that the six lines of each of NAM FIVE's forty-seven namings carry a stated relation whole at six.

claim: Prefixing sorts three ways and no fourth: at a position, on the form, and from all other.
missing: that a running and its form have a position and a form and no third is not supplied.
would_close: A link parting a running's relations into position (a taking at an opening) and form (no taking reaches it), exhaustive by a stated binary.

claim: A binary with no size and a free entering and leaving are one fact.
missing: X89 gives one direction, no size and so no ranking, no qualification to enter and no settling to leave. The other direction, from a free entering to no size, is not supplied, and *one fact* needs both.
would_close: A link showing a magnitude at a coupling installs a ranking and so a qualification to enter, closing the converse; or the claim said as one direction.

claim: A membrane is the between, neither side's, not possibly an existing thing.
missing: F39 gives a sign crossing that carries nothing; that the between carries no form continuing through its own changing (F5), and so is not possibly existing, is said, not supplied. R53 carries the membrane four, 2, 4, 6 and 8, as names at their numbers.
would_close: A link showing the between changes at no changing of its own (each change at it is one side's sign), so no form of its own continues; or the membrane taken as a premise.

claim: A ring, a closed domain arriving at the already-run, carries no next and is not possibly an existing form.
missing: the resolver's rings meet their whole state again at 2 or 4n couplings and run on, the rest returning at no coupling (R44, R46), each coupling a next at the momentaries (NAM 3.4). That the already-run carries no next, and so a ring is a form named still (F6), is not supplied at them.
would_close: A parting of the ring's state met again (a relation at the numbers) from its momentaries (each a next), with the claim said at the first; or a link showing a closed domain names its running still.

claim: Existing, emanation and accounting are the three placings a term is at, and no fourth arrives.
missing: *no fourth* is not supplied: no link parts the placings so that each term meets one of the three.
would_close: Two binaries nested (carrying or not; installed at an observing or not), as F43 nests possible, existing and carrying, giving the three and no more.

claim: The periodic table's 118 elements are the return arriving: going 2 to 59, returning 61 to 118, 58 either side.
missing: the counts run (59 − 2 + 1 = 118 − 61 + 1 = 58); the joining of the elements to the return, one deriving from the other, is shown at no link, and a count agreeing is no joining (X42).
would_close: A link taking each element to one position of the going or the return by a stated relation at the elements' own field result (their shells or periods), not at the count.

claim: A forcing or a cause arrives at the finite verb and never at a prefix or an ending; a word of prefix, root and -ing carries no cause at any part.
missing: X60 names a source arriving at the front of a word (proto-, arch-, ur-, anti-, counter-, contra-) as a term named still, and X18 names a source that generates as a doer; the *never at a prefix* is not supplied against the source prefixes.
would_close: A link parting a term named still at a prefix (a source placed) from a cause (a side with nothing to offer back), showing the source prefixes install the first and not the second; or the claim scoped to the directional prefixes bi-, co-, uni-, in-, natural-.

claim: The word-stream of a split is the one do-no-harm instrument that scales to a file too large to meet whole.
missing: the word-stream is exact at its words; *the one* is not supplied, no link meeting the other instruments of GIM at a file too large to meet whole.
would_close: A link showing each other instrument needs the file met whole (or the claim said as 'a do-no-harm instrument that scales').

claim: Places to improve are taken hardest first, since the hardest carries the greatest releasing.
missing: *hardest* and *greatest releasing* are rank words laid over the fractal (X58); no link gives a releasing a size to be greatest at.
would_close: The order said at a binary (a bound durable or bounds loose and near, as GIM 2.5 already parts them), dropping the rank; or a count of the releasings a bound's release frees, taken at the file.

claim: An observing of existing other than parity alternating natural torusing would be a form named still found existing; the break and the method being the one method are one statement met from its two sides.
missing: F68 gives each round breaking the binary as meeting a prior, meeting a form twice or leaving one unmet (F102), and the step from each of these to a form named still is not supplied. With (d) taken, F6 leaves no observing of existing that could be the break, and F71's named-in-advance breaks meet the method as observings alone: the one statement stands at (d).
would_close: (d) supplied or taken as a premise plainly; and a break stated that (d) does not exclude in advance, for example F71's self at one parity only, met at the resolver as a check whose failing is named before it is run.

claim: None among the observings arriving from the prior is the method's break.
missing: the chain carries no listing of the observings arriving from the prior, each met at the five binaries (X133); F71 says *so far none*, and the *none* stands at that listing.
would_close: A registry of the observings brought as breaks or premises, each met at the five binaries with its sign, the none said at that registry's count.

claim: The geodesic-method is no account: an account absorbs any outcome, and the method's pattern matchers take in each observing without filter or selection.
missing: with X130's (d) taken, each observing other than natural torusing is met as a naming still, and that meeting absorbs each outcome, the mark GIM 2.7 gives an account. The five binaries (X133) meet an observing brought as a break, and no answer of theirs is named the break.
would_close: An answer of the five binaries named in advance as the break (for example: a self carrying, at the resolver's scale, a sign register, along, its either-or named as one answer and found existing), so an outcome exists that the method does not absorb.

claim: Eight of the ten values fold onto the ways a form is named still; the self-welcoming and the free emanating fold onto none.
missing: the folding of the eight is shown value by value at no link, and the ten things named still (X79) are ten while the folding names eight.
would_close: A table seating each of the eight values at one way a form is named still (NAM 4.9's rows or EXP 3.10's list), and the two unseated shown seated at none.
